text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe government has dismissed all junior doctors and nurses who defied a command to return to work on Wednesday after going on strike 10 days ago to press for higher salaries and better working conditions.

- A multi-million dollar deal by the Zimbabwe National Army to buy over 100 trucks from Spain has gone awry, prompting the government to institute legal proceedings against the company involved, Santana Spain, to recover more than Z$200 million.

- The former chief executive of the state-owned Grain Marketing Board (GMB), Renson Gasela, who was suspended 15 months ago on allegations of corruption and lost his job early this week, was however turned into an instant millionaire when government awarded him a Z$2.5 million severance package.

- The shareholders of Northchart Investment Ltd have approved the acquisition of Meikles Consolidated Holdings interests in a landmark decision which will see the largest equity offering ever held by a Zimbabwean-based company.
- Member countries of the Group of 15 developing countries will meet in the Zimbabwean capital Harare over the weekend to discuss, among other issues, the expansion of the grouping.
- The Zimbabwean government said on Wednesday it would award civil servants a bonus in the form of a full 13th cheque this year but warned them it would not tolerate any strike action in future.
- The government owes the state-owned Grain Marketing Board (GMB) over Z$450 million for maize distributed under the grain loan scheme to farmers last year.
